What is the best waterfall on Koh Samui? | For most visitors it is Na Muang 1: free, 5–10 minutes from the car park and with a wide pool you can swim in. Fit walkers who want the biggest drop should add Na Muang 2, a 20–40 minute rope climb to tiers about 80 m high in total.
~Is Na Muang waterfall free? | Yes. Na Muang 1 has no entry fee and the signed left-hand path to Na Muang 2 is free; you pay only for parking, about 20 THB for a scooter and 60 THB for a car at Na Muang 1.
~Can you swim at Na Muang waterfall? | Yes, at Na Muang 1, where an 18 m drop feeds a wide pool. The depth changes suddenly, so check before jumping. Na Muang 2 has only small, slippery plunge pools on the tiers.
How hard is the walk to Na Muang 2? | It is steep and short: 20–40 minutes each way over roots, mud and boulders, with fixed ropes on several sections. Wear grippy closed shoes, go one at a time on the ropes and skip it after heavy rain.
When do Koh Samui's waterfalls have the most water? | October to January, during and just after the north-east monsoon, with November the wettest month at about 445 mm of rain. Late December and January give good flow with safer trails; February to April the falls thin to a trickle.
~How do I get to Na Muang without a scooter? | Take a taxi with an agreed return fare and waiting time, hire a car, or join a 4x4 jungle safari, which includes a Na Muang swim. Grab can drop you off, but getting one back from the waterfall is unreliable and there is no regular songthaew service.
Is Hin Lad waterfall worth it? | Yes, if you are staying on the west side or want a quiet forest walk: about two hours return from the temple trailhead 2–3 km inland from Nathon, with small pools to cool off in. It is less dramatic than Na Muang and very low from February to April.
Are the waterfalls open in the rainy season? | Yes, there are no seasonal closures, but after heavy rain the trails at Na Muang 2 and Hin Lad become slippery and flash floods are possible. On those days swim at Na Muang 1 only and stay out of the stream if the water turns brown or rises.
Which Koh Samui waterfall is best for young children? | Na Muang 1: the walk is flat and shaded, there are toilets and food stalls by the car park, and the edge of the pool is shallow enough for paddling. Na Muang 2 and Hin Lad are not suitable for young children.
Can you visit the Koh Samui waterfalls and the Secret Buddha Garden in one day? | Yes. Start at Na Muang 1 at 09:00, climb Na Muang 2, visit Wat Khunaram after lunch and take a 4x4 up to the Secret Buddha Garden mid-afternoon, finishing at Hin Ta and Hin Yai in Lamai around 17:00.
